summary.intent: Cut per-request `load_verify_locations()` cost for `verify=True` by loading the certifi bundle once into a module-level `SSLContext` that pools reuse, and by no longer setting `ca_certs` on the connection.
summary.issue_fit: Partial. The performance goal is met for plain `verify=True`, but the PR body's promise that `verify=True` keeps behaving as before does not hold once a client certificate is also passed. No originating issue exists; the supplied PR text and commit messages are the intent sources.
summary.coverage: Complete: the single changed file was reviewed against the full merge-base diff, urllib3 2.8.0 callers were read, and one focused pytest selection ran at the head. One candidate and one safety premise were independently verified.

findings.title: Stop loading client certs into the shared default SSLContext
findings.trigger: A `verify=True` request with `cert=('client.pem','client.key')` to one host, then any later `verify=True` request to another host in the same process.
findings.impact: `_urllib3_request_context()` passes the module-level `_preloaded_ssl_context` together with `cert_file`/`key_file`, and urllib3's `ssl_wrap_socket` calls `context.load_cert_chain()` on that shared object. The client identity then stays on the context every later `verify=True` connection uses, so it can be offered to unrelated servers that request client auth, and a different cert later replaces it for handshakes on other threads. At base each pool built its own context, so certs never crossed pools.
findings.change: In `_urllib3_request_context()`, use the shared context only when `client_cert is None`; otherwise set `pool_kwargs["ca_certs"] = extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)` so urllib3 builds a per-pool context and still trusts certifi rather than the OS store.
findings.source: PR body: "verify=True and verify=False still behave as expected".

observations.fact: The shared context is built at import time, so a missing or unreadable certifi bundle now raises when `requests.adapters` is imported, even for `verify=False` users, instead of an `OSError` at request time.
observations.evidence: `src/requests/adapters.py:75-78`; base check in `cert_verify` raised `OSError` per request.

observations.fact: The diff adds no test asserting which certificates the shared context holds or covering `verify=True` together with `cert=`; the author noted they found no way to inspect this.

requirements.source: pr-body/"there is no need to trigger a call to `load_verify_locations()` again"
requirements.evidence: `src/requests/adapters.py:94-95` passes the preloaded context and `cert_verify` (line 298 onward) no longer sets `ca_certs` for `verify=True`.

requirements.source: pr-body/"check that `verify=True` and `verify=False` still behave as expected"
requirements.evidence: Plain verify=True keeps CERT_REQUIRED and hostname checking (verified premise), but with `cert=` the shared context receives `load_cert_chain` (`urllib3/util/ssl_.py:430-433`); see adapters/shared-context-client-cert.

requirements.evidence: Author's timings need network access to a live host and were not repeatable offline; code removes the per-request load_verify_locations call.
